title: A Link Hub on the Drawing Board
author: Jason Lamb
excerpt: An honest starting-point note for the Linktree-inspired folder: the idea is documented, but the planned app files are not there yet.

cover.alt: A Link Hub on the Drawing Board cover image

content_html:
A growing collection of web projects eventually creates another problem: giving people one useful place to find them. The linktree folder in my repository records the start of that idea.

Its README describes a Linktree-inspired landing page and lists planned PHP, CSS, JavaScript, and asset files. In the reviewed snapshot, those application files are not present. This is a project sketch rather than a finished launch.

The interesting question is what a link hub should emphasize. A short list of current destinations can be more useful than a complete inventory of everything ever uploaded. Names need to be understandable, links need clear destinations, and the page needs to work comfortably on a phone. Those are design considerations for the project, not features I am claiming it already has.

The repository also has a separate standalone links-page template, which should not be confused with this planned folder. Keeping that distinction visible is part of documenting a workshop honestly.

For now, this one is an idea with a place to grow. The first meaningful milestone will be a working page that helps someone choose where to go next.
